content.text: The text reviews biliary obstruction, portal-vein thrombosis, liver parasites, pancreatic disease, and peritonitis. Bile-duct blockage causes jaundice, pruritus, pale stools, digestive failure, liver enlargement followed by atrophy, hemorrhage, renal injury, intermittent hepatic fever, and eventual cholaemic coma; causes include stones, inflammation, cancer, parasites, and external compression. Portal thrombosis produces rapid ascites, splenomegaly, abdominal-vein dilation, gastrointestinal bleeding, and usually death; suppurative pylephlebitis causes septic fever and hepatic abscesses. Hydatid cysts enlarge slowly and may obstruct ducts or vessels; aspiration, acupuncture, or surgery were described. Pancreatic disorders cause epigastric-to-back pain, wasting, steatorrhea, jaundice, diabetes, cysts, pancreatitis, and cancer. Peritonitis may follow perforation, gallstones, surgery, infection, tuberculosis, or cancer, producing pain, rigidity, ileus, distension, vomiting, and collapse. Historical treatment emphasized opium, rest, nutrition, drainage, and supportive measures. Cases and physicians are discussed in Bellevue Hospital, Vermont, Philadelphia, London, Paris, and Washington.
